The Northvale Grid Authority said on 12 November 2026 that data center developers have asked to connect 4.8 GW of new load to its transmission system, up from 1.9 GW a year earlier. The figure comes from the authority's quarterly interconnection queue report, which lists 31 data center requests across the region.

Of the 4.8 GW, the report counts 0.9 GW as having signed interconnection agreements. A further 1.4 GW has completed system impact studies. The remaining 2.5 GW is still waiting for its first study. The authority said that studies now take an average of 14 months to complete, compared with 8 months in 2024.

The authority said the transmission system can serve about 1.1 GW of additional load before 2029 without new substations or line upgrades. Projects beyond that amount will need network upgrades whose cost is assigned to the requesting customers. The report estimates those upgrades at $2.3 billion for the requests now in the queue, and it does not say how that cost would be shared among projects that share a substation.

Developers have asked the authority for faster processing. The report says the authority will introduce a readiness deposit of $50,000 per megawatt for new requests from 1 March 2027, refundable when a project reaches commercial operation. Requests that cannot show site control will be removed from the queue, and the authority expects that rule to remove some speculative requests.

The authority also published its load forecast. It expects peak demand on its system to grow by 18 percent by 2031, with AI data center campuses accounting for most of the increase. It said that forecast assumes only the 0.9 GW with signed agreements will be built on schedule, and that requests without agreements are treated as uncertain.

The report notes that two large campuses account for 1.6 GW of the queued requests. Both are planned for AI training and inference workloads, according to their filings, and both are seeking project financing. Neither has a signed interconnection agreement, and neither appears in the 1.1 GW the authority says it can serve without upgrades.

The authority will hold a stakeholder meeting on the readiness deposit in January 2027 and publish its next queue report in February 2027. It did not give energization dates for any of the requests in the queue.
